Primary request: PRESSED GLASS, symbolised by a 19th-century HAND-LEVER GLASS PRESS with its mould. ONE main connected apparatus in FLAT FRONT/SIDE ELEVATION: a simple sturdy C-shaped press frame on a low broad foot; an upper angled hand lever attached to the frame's pivot and connected to ONE thick vertical plunger; beneath the plunger ONE large short open bowl-shaped metal mould mounted on the same base. The plunger is aligned over the mould's interior, almost engaging it, with a conspicuous transparent gap. Use a thick upper lever angled upward, broad frame and strong few components. The mould is wide, its cavity suggested by ONE simple U-shaped inset line, no perspective top ellipse or glass shine. This is pressing hot glass into a mould, NOT a printing press, screw press, book, paper stack or forge hammer. No screw threads, separate finished glass, steam, flame or extra output object. All parts the SAME beige/ochre family.
